nodes.name: Proposition 4.11: Prop
nodes.statement:
Consider two tensors $h_{k_{A_1}}^{(1)}$ and $h_{k_{A_2}}^{(2)}$, where $A_1\cap A_2=C$. Let $A_1\Delta A_2=A$, define the semi-product
 \begin{equation}H_{k_A}=\sum_{k_C}h_{k_{A_1}}^{(1)}h_{k_{A_2}}^{(2)}.
 \end{equation} Then, for any partition $(X,Y)$ of $A$, let $X\cap A_1=X_1$, $Y\cap A_1 =Y_1$ etc., we have
 \begin{equation}\|H\|_{k_X\to k_Y}\leq \|h^{(1)}\|_{k_{X_1\cup C}\to k_{Y_1}}\cdot\|h^{(2)}\|_{k_{X_2}\to k_{C\cup Y_2}}.
 \end{equation}

nodes.name: Proposition 4.12: Prop
nodes.statement:
Let $A_j\,(1\leq j\leq m)$ be index sets, such that any index appears in at most two $A_j$'s, and let $h^{(j)}=h_{k_{A_j}}^{(j)}$ be tensors. Let $A=A_1\Delta\cdots\Delta A_m$ be the set of indices that belong to only one $A_j$, and $C=(A_1\cup\cdots \cup A_m)\backslash A$ be the set of indices that belong to two different $A_j$'s. Define the semi-product
 \begin{equation}H_{k_A}=\sum_{k_C}\prod_{j=1}^mh_{k_{A_j}}^{(j)}.
 \end{equation} Let $(X,Y)$ be a partition of $A$. For $1\leq j\leq m$ let $X_j=X\cap A_j$ and $Y_j=Y\cap A_j$, and define
 \begin{equation}B_j:=\bigcup_{\ell>j}(A_j\cap A_\ell),\quad C_j=\bigcup_{\ell<j}(A_j\cap A_\ell),
 \end{equation} then we have
 \begin{equation}\|H\|_{k_X\to k_Y}\leq\prod_{j=1}^m\|h^{(j)}\|_{k_{X_j\cup B_j}\to k_{Y_j\cup C_j}}.
 \end{equation}

nodes.name: Lemma 4.4
nodes.statement:
Let $E\subset \mathbb{Z}^d$ be a finite set, $a=a_{k_1\cdots k_r}(\omega)$ be a random tensor such that the collection $\{a_{k_1\cdots k_r}\}$ is independent with the collection $\{\eta_k(\omega):k\in E\}$. Let $\zeta_j\in\{\pm\}$ and assume that in the support of $a_{k_1\cdots k_r}$ there is no pairing in $(k_1,\cdots,k_r)$ associated with the signs $\zeta_j$. Let the random variable
 \begin{equation}X(\omega):=\sum_{k_1,\cdots,k_r}a_{k_1\cdots k_r}(\omega)\prod_{j=1}^r\eta_j(\omega)^{\zeta_j},
 \end{equation} then for any $A>0$, we have $A$-certainly that
 \begin{equation}|X(\omega)|^2\leq A^\theta\cdot\sum_{k_1,\cdots,k_r}|a_{k_1\cdots k_r}(\omega)|^2.
 \end{equation}

nodes.name: Lemma 4.5, Lemma 4.8: Lem --
nodes.statement:
Consider the set
 \begin{multline}S^{(3)}=\big\{(k_1,k_2,k_3)\in(\mathbb{Z}^d)^3:\zeta_1k_1+\zeta_2k_2+\zeta_3k_3=m,\,\,\zeta_1|k_1|^2+\zeta_2|k_2|^2+\zeta_3|k_3|^2=\Gamma,
 \\|k_1-m_1|\leq M_1,\,\,|k_2-m_2|\leq M_2,\,\,\text{\rm{and there is no pairing in $(k_1,k_2,k_3)$}}\big\},
 \end{multline} where $\zeta_j\in\{\pm\}$, $(m,\Gamma)\in\mathbb{Z}^d\times\mathbb{Z}$, $m_j\in\mathbb{Z}^d$ and $M_j$ dyadic are given. Then we have, uniformly in all parameters, that
 \begin{equation}\#S^{(3)}\lesssim (M_1M_2)^{d-1+\theta}.
 \end{equation}

Consider the same setting and set $S$ as in Lemma 4.7, but instead of no pairing in $k_A$ we assume that (1) any pairing in $k_A$ must be over-paired, and (2) $d(p-1)\geq 8$. Then the bound (4.16) remains true.

nodes.name: Proposition 4.9: Prop
nodes.statement:
Partition $\{1,\cdots,p\}$ into disjoint nonempty subsets $A_1,\cdots,A_s$, $B_1,\cdots,B_t$ and $C$. Assume $A_v=\{\ell_v(1),\cdots ,\ell_v(a_v)\}$, $B_u=\{i_u(1),\cdots ,i_u(b_u)\}$, and $C=\{n_1,\cdots, n_c=1\}$. Consider a tensor $h=h_{kk_1\cdots k_p}$, where each $k,k_j\in\mathbb{Z}^d$, which satisfies $|h_{kk_1\cdots k_p}|\lesssim 1$, and in the support of $h$ we have (with $m_j\in\mathbb{Z}^d$ fixed)
  \begin{equation}\sum_{j\in A_v}\zeta_j|k_j|^2=\Gamma_v,\quad\bigg|\sum_{z=1}^y\zeta_{\ell_v(z)}k_{\ell_v(z)}-m_{\ell_v(y)}\bigg|\leq M_{\ell_u(y)},\,\forall 1\leq v\leq s,1\leq y\leq a_v=|A_v|.
 \end{equation}
   \begin{equation}\sum_{j=1}^p\zeta_j|k_j|^2-|k|^2=\Gamma,\quad \bigg|\sum_{z=1}^y\zeta_{i_u(z)}k_{i_u(z)}-m_{i_u(y)}\bigg|\leq M_{i_u(y)},\,\forall 1\leq u\leq t,1\leq y\leq b_u=|B_u|,
 \end{equation}
    \begin{equation}\bigg|\sum_{z=1}^y\zeta_{n_z}k_{n_z}-m_{n_y}\bigg|\leq M_{n_y},\,\forall 1\leq y\leq c-1=|C|-1.
 \end{equation} We assume that $M_{\ell_v(a_v)}=M_{i_u(b_u)}=1$ (denote also $M_{n_c}=1$), and that
 \begin{equation}\sum_{j\in A_v}\zeta_j=0\,(\forall 1\leq v\leq s),\,\,\sum_{j=1}^p\zeta_j=1;\quad\sum_{j=1}^p\zeta_jk_j-k=\sum_{j\in A_v}\zeta_jk_j=0.\end{equation} We also assume that any pairing in $(k,k_1,\cdots,k_p)$ is over-paired. Then, for any subset $P_0$ satisfying $P_0\subset C\backslash\{1\}$, let $\{1,\cdots,p\}\backslash P_0=Q_0$, then we have
 \begin{equation}\|h\|_{kk_{P_0}\to k_{Q_0}}\lesssim \prod_{j=2}^{p}(M_j)^{\alpha_0+\theta}\prod_{v=1}^s(\min_{1\leq y<a_v}M_{\ell_v(y)})^{\alpha_0-\frac{d}{2}},
 \end{equation} \emph{unless} $(d,p)=(1,7)$, and (up to permutation) that $|A_1|=|A_2|=2$, $k_{\ell_1(1)}=k_{\ell_2(1)}$.
 
Furthermore, if we do not assume that $h$ is supported in the set $\sum_{j=1}^p\zeta_j|k_j|^2-|k|^2=\Gamma$ as in (4.23), but instead assume 
\begin{equation}|h_{k_1\cdots k_p}|\lesssim\frac{1}{\langle \Omega+\Gamma\rangle},\quad \Omega:=|k|^2-\sum_{j=1}^p\zeta_j|k_j|^2,\end{equation}then the same result holds. Finally, all the above results remain true if we replace $p$ by any odd $3\leq q\leq p$ (without changing the value of $\alpha_0$).

nodes.name: Proposition 6.2, Proposition 6.3: Prop --
Proposition 4.14, Proposition 4.15: Prop
nodes.statement:
Let $A$ be a finite set and $h_{bck_A}=h_{bck_A}(\omega)$ be a tensor, where each $k_j\in \mathbb{Z}^d$ and $(b,c)\in (\mathbb{Z}^d)^q$ for some integer $q\geq 2$. Given signs $\zeta_j\in\{\pm\}$, we also assume that $\langle b\rangle,\langle c\rangle\lesssim M$ and $\langle k_j\rangle\lesssim M$ for all $j\in A$, where $M$ is a dyadic number, and that in the support of $h_{bck_A}$ there is no pairing in $k_A$. Define the tensor
  \begin{equation}
  H_{bc}=\sum_{k_{A}}h_{bck_A}\prod_{j\in A}\eta_{k_j}^{\zeta_j},
  \end{equation}where we restrict $k_j\in E$ in (4.35), $E$ being a finite set such that $\{h_{bck_A}\}$ is independent with $\{\eta_k:k\in E\}$. Then $\tau^{-1}M$-certainly, we have
  \begin{equation}\|H_{bc}\|_{b\to c}\lesssim\tau^{-\theta} M^\theta\cdot\max_{(B,C)}\|h\|_{bk_B\to ck_C},
  \end{equation} where $(B,C)$ runs over all partitions of $A$.

Consider the same setting as in Proposition 4.14, with the following differences: (1) we only restrict $\langle k_j\rangle\lesssim M$ but do not impose any condition on $\langle b\rangle$ or $\langle c\rangle$; (2) we assume $b,c\in\mathbb{Z}^d$ also, and assume that in the support of $h_{bck_A}$ we have $|b-\zeta c|\lesssim M$ where $\zeta\in\{\pm\}$; (3) the tensor $h_{bck_A}$ only depends on $b-\zeta c$, $|b|^2-\zeta |c|^2$ and $k_A$, and is supported in the set where $||b|^2-\zeta|c|^2|\leq M^{\kappa^3}$. The other assumptions are the same. Then $\tau^{-1}M$-certainly we have
  \begin{equation*}\|H_{bc}\|_{b\to c}\lesssim \tau^{-\theta}M^\theta\cdot\sup_{(B,C)}\|h\|_{bk_B\to ck_C}.
  \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Proposition 6.1: Prop
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathcal{S}$ be a regular plant, $N(\mathcal{S})=N\leq M$ and $|\mathcal{S}|\leq D$. Let $h=h_{kk_{\mathcal{U}}}(k_{\mathcal{V}},\lambda_{\mathcal{V}})$ be an $\mathcal{S}$-tensor which is $\mathcal{B}_{N^{[\delta]}}$ measurable. For $N^\delta\leq R\leq M^\delta$, consider the trimmed plant $\mathcal{S}'=(\mathcal{L}',\mathcal{V}',\mathcal{Y}')=\mathrm{Trim}(\mathcal{S},R)$ and the trimmed tensor $h'=(h')_{kk_{\mathcal{U}'}}(k_{\mathcal{V}'},\lambda_{\mathcal{V}'})=\mathtt{Trim}(h,R)$. Let $(B,C)$ be a subpartition of $\mathcal{U}$ with $E=\mathcal{U}\backslash(B\cup C)$ and $(B',C')$ be a subpartition of $\mathcal{U}'$ with $E'=\mathcal{U}'\backslash(B'\cup C')$.
  
  (1) Assume $h$ satisfies that, for any $(B,C)$ with $C\neq\varnothing$,
  \begin{equation}\|h_{kk_{\mathcal{U}}}(k_{\mathcal{V}},\lambda_{\mathcal{V}})\|_{X_{\mathcal{V}}^{-b_0}[kk_B\to k_C]}\lesssim\mathfrak{X}\cdot\prod_{\mathfrak{l}\in B\cup C}N_{\mathfrak{l}}^\beta\prod_{\mathfrak{l}\in\mathcal{P}}N_{\mathfrak{l}}^{-4\varepsilon}\prod_{\mathfrak{l}\in E}N_{\mathfrak{l}}^{8\varepsilon}\prod_{\mathfrak{p}\in\mathcal{Y}}N_{\mathfrak{p}}^{-\delta^3}\prod_{\mathfrak{f} \in \mathcal{V}} N_{\mathfrak{f}}^d\cdot \big(\max_{\mathfrak{l}\in C}N_{\mathfrak{l}}\big)^{-\beta},
  \end{equation} and for $C=\varnothing$,
  \begin{equation}
 \|h_{kk_{\mathcal{U}}}(k_{\mathcal{V}},\lambda_{\mathcal{V}})\|_{X_{\mathcal{V}}^{-b_0}[kk_B]}\lesssim\mathfrak{X}\cdot\prod_{\mathfrak{l}\in B}N_{\mathfrak{l}}^\beta\prod_{\mathfrak{l}\in\mathcal{P}}N_{\mathfrak{l}}^{-4\varepsilon}\prod_{\mathfrak{l}\in E}N_{\mathfrak{l}}^{8\varepsilon}\prod_{\mathfrak{p}\in\mathcal{Y}}N_{\mathfrak{p}}^{-\delta^3}\prod_{\mathfrak{f} \in \mathcal{V}} N_{\mathfrak{f}}^d\cdot N^{-\varepsilon},
 \end{equation}
 \begin{equation} \bigg\|\bigg(1+\frac{1}{N^{2\delta}}\big|k-\sum_{\mathfrak{l}\in\mathcal{U}}\zeta_{\mathfrak{l}} k_{\mathfrak{l}}-\ell\big|\bigg)^\kappa h_{kk_{\mathcal{U}}}(k_{\mathcal{V}},\lambda_{\mathcal{V}})\bigg\|_{X_{\mathcal{V}}^{-b_0}[kk_B]}\lesssim\mathfrak{X}\cdot\prod_{\mathfrak{l}\in B}N_{\mathfrak{l}}^\beta\prod_{\mathfrak{l}\in\mathcal{P}}N_{\mathfrak{l}}^{-4\varepsilon}\prod_{\mathfrak{l}\in E}N_{\mathfrak{l}}^{8\varepsilon}\prod_{\mathfrak{p}\in\mathcal{Y}}N_{\mathfrak{p}}^{-\delta^3}\prod_{\mathfrak{f} \in \mathcal{V}} N_{\mathfrak{f}}^d,
 \end{equation} where $\ell=\sum_{\mathfrak{f}\in\mathcal{V}}\zeta_{\mathfrak{f}} k_{\mathfrak{f}}$, and also the auxiliary bound for $C=E=\varnothing$,
 \begin{equation}\|\partial_{\lambda_{\mathcal{V}}}h_{kk_{\mathcal{U}}}(k_{\mathcal{V}},\lambda_{\mathcal{V}})\|_{X_{\mathcal{V}}^{-b_0}[kk_{\mathcal{U}}]}\leq\mathfrak{X}\cdot\exp[(\log N)^5+|\mathcal{S}|(\log N)^3].
 \end{equation} Then, $\tau^{-1}M$-certainly, the estimates (6.1)--(6.3) hold for $h=h_{kk_{\mathcal{U}}}(k_{\mathcal{V}},\lambda_{\mathcal{V}})$ replaced by $h'=h_{kk_{\mathcal{U}'}}'(k_{\mathcal{V}'},\lambda_{\mathcal{V}'})$, the sets $B,C,E,\mathcal{P},\mathcal{V}$ etc. replaced by $B',C',E',\mathcal{P}',\mathcal{V}'$ etc., the fraction $1/N^{2\delta}$ in (6.3) replaced by $1/\max(N^{2\delta},R)$, and the factor $\mathfrak{X}$ replaced by $\mathfrak{X}\cdot\tau^{-\theta}M^\theta$.
 
 (2) Assume $\mathcal{V}=\varnothing$, $h$ is supported in the set $k=\sum_{\mathfrak{l}\in\mathcal{U}}\zeta_{\mathfrak{l}} k_{\mathfrak{l}}$ and satisfies that, for any $(B,C)$,
 \begin{equation}
 \|h_{kk_{\mathcal{U}}}\|_{kk_B\to k_C}\leq\mathfrak{X}\cdot \prod_{\mathfrak{l}\in B\cup C}N_{\mathfrak{l}}^{\beta_1}\prod_{\mathfrak{l}\in\mathcal{P}}N_{\mathfrak{l}}^{-8\varepsilon}\prod_{\mathfrak{l}\in E}N_{\mathfrak{l}}^{4\varepsilon}\prod_{\mathfrak{p}\in\mathcal{Y}}N_{\mathfrak{p}}^{-\delta^3}\cdot\mathcal{X}_0\mathcal{X}_1,
 \end{equation} where $\mathcal{X}_0$ and $\mathcal{X}_1$ are defined as in (5.33). Assume also that either $C'\cup E'\neq\varnothing$, or $\mathcal{L}\neq\mathcal{L}'$ (i.e. $N_{\mathfrak{l}}<R$ for at least one $\mathfrak{l}\in\mathcal{L}$), then $\tau^{-1}M$-certainly, the estimates (6.1)--(6.3) hold for $h'=h_{kk_{\mathcal{U}'}}'$, with the sets $B,C,E,\mathcal{P}$ etc. replaced by $B',C',E',\mathcal{P}'$ etc., the fraction $1/N^{2\delta}$ in (6.3) replaced by $1/R$, and the factor $\mathfrak{X}$ replaced by $\mathfrak{X}\cdot \tau^{-\theta}M^\theta $ for (6.1), and by $\mathfrak{X}\cdot \tau^{-\theta}M^\theta (1+N^{-3\varepsilon}R^{d/2-\beta_1})$ for (6.2)--(6.3).

nodes.name: Proposition 6.4, Proposition 6.6: Prop --
Proposition 7.1, Proposition 7.4: Prop --
nodes.statement:
Assume $\mathtt{Local}(M)$ is true. Then $\|\mathscr{L}^{M,\zeta}\|_{X^{1-b}\to X^{b}}\leq\tau^{(6\kappa)^{-1}}$ for $\zeta\in\{\pm\}$, so in particular $\mathscr{R}^M=(1-\mathscr{L}^M)^{-1}$ and $\|\mathscr{V}^{M,\zeta}\|_{X^{1-b}\to X^b}\leq \tau^{(7\kappa)^{-1}}$. For the kernel $\mathscr{L}^{M,\zeta}$ we also have
\begin{equation}\int_{\mathbb{R}}\langle\lambda\rangle^{2(1-b)}\|\langle\lambda'\rangle^{-(1-b)}(\widehat{\mathscr{L}^{M,\zeta}})_{kk'}(\lambda,\lambda')\|_{\ell_{k'}^2L_{\lambda'}^2\to \ell_k^2}^2\,\mathrm{d}\lambda\leq\tau^{(3\kappa)^{-1}},
\end{equation} and the same bound (7.1) holds also for the kernel $\mathscr{V}^{M,\zeta}$, with the power $(3\kappa)^{-1}$ on the right hand side replaced by $(7\kappa/2)^{-1}$. Moreover for any $\widetilde{N}$ we have
\begin{equation}\|\mathbf{1}_{\langle k'\rangle\leq \widetilde{N}}(\mathscr{V}^{M,\zeta})_{kk'}\|_{X^{b,-(1-b)}[kk']}\leq \tau^{(8\kappa)^{-1}}(\widetilde{N})^{\alpha_0}\cdot M^{C\delta},
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}\|(1+M^{-\delta}|k-\zeta k'|)^{\kappa^2}(\mathscr{V}^{M,\zeta})_{kk'}\|_{X^{b,-(1-b)}[k k']}\leq \tau^{(8\kappa)^{-1}}M^{\beta_1-\varepsilon}.
\end{equation}

Assume $\mathtt{Local}(M)$ and parts (1) and (2) of $\mathtt{Local}(2M)$ are true. Then $\tau^{-1}M$-certainly, parts (3)--(5) of $\mathtt{Local}(2M)$ are true. More precisely, (5.38) is true for each $n\in\{0,1\}$ and regular plant $\mathcal{S}$ with $N(\mathcal{S})=M$ and $|\mathcal{S}|\leq D$, and the mapping that defines $z_M$ (see the right hand side of (5.28)) is a contraction mapping from the ball $\{z:\|z\|_{X^{b_0}}\leq M^{-D_1}\}$ to itself, and (5.40) is true for the kernel $\mathscr{L}^{\zeta}$ defined by (5.39), if $\max(N_2,\cdots,N_q)=M$.

nodes.name: Proposition 5.1: Prop
nodes.statement:
Given a dyadic $M$, consider the following set of statements (viewed as an event for $\omega$), which we shall refer to as $\mathtt{Local}(M)$ below: 

(1) For any plain regular plant $\mathcal{S}=(\mathcal{L},\varnothing,\mathcal{Y})$ with $N(\mathcal{S})=N< M$ and $|\mathcal{S}|\leq D$, we have that
\begin{equation} h^{(\mathcal{S},0)}=h_{kk_{\mathcal{U}}}^{(\mathcal{S},0)}(t)\mathrm{\ is\ supported\ in\ the\ set\ where\ }k=\sum_{\mathfrak{l}\in\mathcal{U}}\zeta_{\mathfrak{l}} k_{\mathfrak{l}}.
\end{equation}For any $\Gamma\in\mathbb{Z}$, let $h^{(\mathcal{S},0,\Gamma)}$ be the restriction of $h^{(\mathcal{S},0)}$ to the set where
 \begin{equation} |k|^2-\sum_{\mathfrak{l}\in\mathcal{U}}\zeta_{\mathfrak{l}}|k_{\mathfrak{l}}|^2=\Gamma,
 \end{equation} obtained by multiplying by the indicator function of this set. Let $(B,C)$ be a subpartition of $\mathcal{U}$ and let $E=\mathcal{U}\backslash(B\cup C)$. Then we have
 \begin{equation}\int_{\mathbb{R}}\langle \lambda\rangle^{2b}\bigg(\sum_{\Gamma\in\mathbb{Z}}\|\widehat{h_{kk_{\mathcal{U}}}^{(\mathcal{S},0,\Gamma)}}(\lambda)\|_{kk_B\to k_C}\bigg)^2\,\mathrm{d}\lambda\leq\bigg(\prod_{\mathfrak{l}\in B\cup C}N_{\mathfrak{l}}^{\beta_1}\prod_{\mathfrak{l}\in\mathcal{P}}N_{\mathfrak{l}}^{-8\varepsilon}\prod_{\mathfrak{l}\in E}N_{\mathfrak{l}}^{4\varepsilon}\prod_{\mathfrak{p}\in\mathcal{Y}}N_{\mathfrak{p}}^{-\delta^3}\cdot\mathcal{X}_0\mathcal{X}_1\bigg)^2,
 \end{equation} with the quantities
 \begin{equation}\mathcal{X}_0=\left\{
  \begin{aligned}&\big(\max_{\mathfrak{l}\in C}N_{\mathfrak{l}}\big)^{-\beta_1},&&\mathrm{if\ }C\neq\varnothing;\\
    & \big(\min_{\mathfrak{l}\in\mathcal{L}}N_{\mathfrak{l}}\big)^{\frac{d}{2}-\beta_1},&&\mathrm{if\ }C=E=\varnothing;\\
   & N^{-\varepsilon\delta},&&\mathrm{if\ }B=C=\varnothing;\\
    &1,&&\mathrm{otherwise},
 \end{aligned}
 \right.\qquad\mathcal{X}_1=\left\{
 \begin{aligned}&1,&{\rm{if }}\max_{\mathfrak{l}\in \mathcal{L}}N_{\mathfrak{l}}&\geq (10^3dp)^{-|\mathcal{L}|}N;\\
&N^{-4\varepsilon},&{\rm{if }}\max_{\mathfrak{l}\in \mathcal{L}}N_{\mathfrak{l}}&< (10^3dp)^{-|\mathcal{L}|}N.
 \end{aligned}
 \right.
 \end{equation}
 
 (2) For any regular plant $\mathcal{S}=(\mathcal{L},\mathcal{V},\mathcal{Y})$ with $N(\mathcal{S})=N< M$ and $|\mathcal{S}|\leq D$, consider the tensor $h^{(\mathcal{S},1)}=h_{kk_{\mathcal{U}}}^{(\mathcal{S},1)}(t,k_{\mathcal{V}},\lambda_{\mathcal{V}})$. Let $(B,C)$ be a subpartition of $\mathcal{U}$ and let $E=\mathcal{U}\backslash(B\cup C)$. Then, recall the norms defined in (3.17)--(3.18), for $C\neq\varnothing$ we have \begin{equation}\|h_{kk_{\mathcal{U}}}^{(\mathcal{S},1)}(t,k_{\mathcal{V}},\lambda_{\mathcal{V}})\|_{X_{\mathcal{V}}^{1-b,-b_0}[kk_B\to k_C]}\leq\prod_{\mathfrak{l}\in B\cup C}N_{\mathfrak{l}}^\beta\prod_{\mathfrak{l}\in\mathcal{P}}N_{\mathfrak{l}}^{-4\varepsilon}\prod_{\mathfrak{l}\in E}N_{\mathfrak{l}}^{8\varepsilon}\prod_{\mathfrak{p}\in\mathcal{Y}}N_{\mathfrak{p}}^{-\delta^3}\prod_{\mathfrak{f} \in \mathcal{V}} N_{\mathfrak{f}}^d
 \cdot 
\big(\max_{\mathfrak{l}\in C}N_{\mathfrak{l}}\big)^{-\beta},
 \end{equation} while for $C=\varnothing$ we have
 \begin{equation}
 \|h_{kk_{\mathcal{U}}}^{(\mathcal{S},1)}(t,k_{\mathcal{V}},\lambda_{\mathcal{V}})\|_{X_{\mathcal{V}}^{\widetilde{b},-b_0}[kk_B]}\leq\prod_{\mathfrak{l}\in B}N_{\mathfrak{l}}^\beta\prod_{\mathfrak{l}\in\mathcal{P}}N_{\mathfrak{l}}^{-4\varepsilon}\prod_{\mathfrak{l}\in E}N_{\mathfrak{l}}^{8\varepsilon}\prod_{\mathfrak{p}\in\mathcal{Y}}N_{\mathfrak{p}}^{-\delta^3}\prod_{\mathfrak{f} \in \mathcal{V}} N_{\mathfrak{f}}^d\cdot N^{-\varepsilon},
 \end{equation} where $\widetilde{b}$ equals $1-b$ if $E\neq \varnothing$ and equals $b$ if $E=\varnothing$. We also have a localization bound (for $C=\varnothing$)
 \begin{equation} \bigg\|\bigg(1+\frac{1}{N^{2\delta}}\big|k-\sum_{\mathfrak{l}\in\mathcal{U}}\zeta_{\mathfrak{l}} k_{\mathfrak{l}}-\ell\big|\bigg)^\kappa h_{kk_{\mathcal{U}}}^{(\mathcal{S},1)}(t,k_{\mathcal{V}},\lambda_{\mathcal{V}})\bigg\|_{X_{\mathcal{V}}^{\widetilde{b},-b_0}[kk_B]}\leq\prod_{\mathfrak{l}\in B}N_{\mathfrak{l}}^\beta\prod_{\mathfrak{l}\in\mathcal{P}}N_{\mathfrak{l}}^{-4\varepsilon}\prod_{\mathfrak{l}\in E}N_{\mathfrak{l}}^{8\varepsilon}\prod_{\mathfrak{p}\in\mathcal{Y}}N_{\mathfrak{p}}^{-\delta^3}\prod_{\mathfrak{f} \in \mathcal{V}} N_{\mathfrak{f}}^d,
 \end{equation} where $\ell=\sum_{\mathfrak{f}\in\mathcal{V}}\zeta_{\mathfrak{f}} k_{\mathfrak{f}}$, and $\widetilde{b}$ is the one in (5.35).
 
 Finally, we have an auxiliary bound for the $\lambda_{\mathcal{V}}$-derivative\footnote{Note that, once we have (5.37), we automatically have the same bound for the norm with the weight in (5.36), with the right hand side multiplied by $N^\kappa$, which is negligible as the right hand side is super-polynomial.} of $h_{kk_{\mathcal{U}}}^{(\mathcal{S},1)}(t,k_{\mathcal{V}},\lambda_{\mathcal{V}})$ (for $C=E=\varnothing$),
  \begin{equation} \|\partial_{\lambda_{\mathcal{V}}}h_{kk_{\mathcal{U}}}^{(\mathcal{S},1)}(t,k_{\mathcal{V}},\lambda_{\mathcal{V}})\|_{X_{\mathcal{V}}^{b,-b_0}[kk_{\mathcal{U}}]}\leq \exp[(\log N)^5+|\mathcal{S}|(\log N)^3].
 \end{equation}
 
 (3) For $n\in\{0,1\}$ and regular plant $\mathcal{S}$ with $N(\mathcal{S})=N<M$ and $|\mathcal{S}|\leq D$, let the expression $\Psi_{k}^{(\mathcal{S},n)}=\Psi_k[\mathcal{S},h^{(\mathcal{S},n)}]$ be defined as in (3.8), then we have
 \begin{equation}\|\Psi^{(\mathcal{S},n)}\|_{X^{s',b_0}}\leq\tau^{-\theta_0}N^{s'-s}\prod_{\mathfrak{n}\in\mathcal{L}\cup\mathcal{V}\cup\mathcal{Y}}N_{\mathfrak{n}}^{-\delta^3}
 \end{equation} for any $s-\delta^2<s'<s$, where $(s,b_0,\theta_0)$ are defined in (1.3) and Section 3.1.
 
  (4) For all $N<M$, the mapping that defines $z_N$ (namely the right hand side of (5.28) but with $M$ replaced by $N$ and then $z_N$ replaced by an independent variable $z$) is a contraction mapping from $\{z:\|z\|_{X^{b_0}}\leq N^{-D_1}\}$ to itself with $D_1$ as in (3.3). In particular, we have $\|z_N\|_{X^{b_0}}\leq N^{-D_1}$ for all $N<M$.
 
 (5) Let $y_{N}$ and $v_{N}^\dagger$ be defined as in (5.17) for $N<M$, then they solve the system (5.16) for $N<M$. Moreover, for any $N_2,\cdots,N_{q}< M$ and any $N$ (which may be $\geq M$), consider the operator $\mathscr{L}^\zeta$ (which is complex linear if $\zeta=+$, and conjugate complex linear if $\zeta=-$) defined by
 \begin{equation}(\mathscr{L}^\zeta w)_k(t)=\chi_\tau(t)\cdot\mathcal{I}_\chi\Pi_N\mathcal{M}_q(y_{N_2}^*,\cdots,w,\cdots, y_{N_{q}}^*)_k(t),
 \end{equation} and the corresponding kernel $(\mathscr{L}^\zeta)_{kk'}(t,t')$, where each $y_{N_j}^*$ is either $y_{N_j}$ or one of its components, namely $z_{N_j}$ (possibly with Fourier truncations similar to the ones in $z_N^{\mathrm{hi}}$ and $z_N^{\mathrm{lo}}$ defined in Section 5.2) or $\Psi[\mathcal{S}_j,h^{(\mathcal{S}_j,n_j)}]$ for some $n_j\in\{0,1\}$ and regular plant $\mathcal{S}_j$ with $N(\mathcal{S}_j)=N_j$ and $|\mathcal{S}_j|\leq D$ (see (3.8) and (5.17)), then they satisfy
 \begin{equation}\|\mathscr{L}^\zeta\|_{X^{1-b,-b}[k\to k']}\leq \tau^{(5\kappa)^{-1}}\big(\max_{2\leq j\leq q}N_j\big)^{-4\varepsilon\delta}.
 \end{equation}
 
Now, with the above definition of $\mathtt{Local}(M)$, we have that \emph{the probability that $\mathtt{Local}(M)$ holds but $\mathtt{Local}(2M)$ does not hold} is $\leq C_\theta e^{-(\tau^{-1}M)^\theta}$. In particular, $\tau^{-1}$-certainly, $\mathtt{Local}(M)$ holds for all $M$.
  }}

nodes.name: Theorem 1.1
Theorem 1.6
